name: Pack Ice
desc: A drifting ice pack failing from altitude — the plate breaks along conjugate shear lines, so wherever the wind pulls it apart a lead rips open to black water and immediately starts skinning over with dark nilas, and wherever it shoves back together the floes raft and pressure ridges pile up bright and throw long blue shadows under a sun that never rises; true-colour aerial survey, speckled radar backscatter, close nilas with frost flowers, rotten summer ice pooling cyan, or a flat ice-chart classification.

energy.doc: how hard the wind works the pack — divergent forcing, lead-opening rate and tonal gain; max tears the plate apart

scale.doc: altitude — max drops nearly three times closer about the x/y anchor

speed.doc: drift rate of the whole pack (0.2 still deforms, never freezes into a picture)

density.doc: how many conjugate fracture lines the plate is allowed to fail along — few long leads or a busy shattered mosaic

freeze.doc: how fast open water skins over — low keeps leads black and gaping, high heals them to grey ice almost as they open

hue.doc: hue of the light on the snow — the water and nilas stay cold underneath

x.doc: horizontal position of the magnified region

y.doc: vertical position of the magnified region

style.doc: aesthetic: true-colour aerial survey under a low sun / synthetic-aperture radar backscatter, speckled greyscale, smooth ice dark and ridges blazing / close on dark young nilas blooming frost flowers / rotten summer ice pooling with cyan melt ponds / flat false-colour ice-chart classification with hatched ridging

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the initial floe field and the fracture-line geometry
